[b]|+|A Praça da Reforma, Nossa Senhora de Olorença|+|[/b]
  [u][b][/b]‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ [/u]
[b][sub]|:| [i]Viñeron do mar[/i] |:|[/sub][/b]

Have you ever wondered what a piece of heaven might look like on Earth? Well, look no further than the city of Olorença. People from all walks of life have praised the beautiful architecture, which proudly stands bold amid the modern age. Olorença was noted for its many traditional Mediterranean buildings blended with Neo-Colonial styles that dotted the landscape. Their Sun-kissed stones gleamed, and the cobbled paths glimmered like gems in the Mediterranean sun. Many of the ornate buildings were home to the Citizens of Olorença. Many more shuffled in and out of their domiciles, while others came from shops, and some enjoyed access to the natural preserves that surrounded the rolling hills of the Capital. Oh, how Olorença pulsated with life in every moment. Overall, it was just an entirely different feel from the rest of the country. You could tell that it stood the test of time as being the heart of the nation amidst contenders. Olorença continuously improves around every corner according to the agendas of Officials.

[sub][i]```Chorando se foi quem um dia só me fez chorar
Chorando se foi quem um dia só me fez chorar...```[/i][/sub]

Indeed, the waking hours of the city never seemed to stop. Especially so with the boundless energy, which radiates at a constant rate, it was overwhelmingly contagious. Sheltered or more tranquil areas of Olorença were more appealing to me. Quiet cafés to be precise. It always made those monotonous days bearable. Peers, although not many, would not agree with me. They were from a different cloth. Those [i]folks[/i], if you will. If you asked my brother, he would have been quite fervent. He was a bit of a patriot to be light, but I admired that sense of patriotism.

[sub][i]```Chorando estará ao lembrar de um amor
Que um dia não soube cuidar
Chorando estará ao lembrar de um amor
Que um dia não soube cuidar...```[/i][/sub]

Funny, how we can remember events more, but periodic days feel less tranquil than in the past. The origins may be no mystery after all. I do recall a day when estranxeiros arrived from afar. Funny little thingsthey brought with them their culture, trinkets, and smells, yet their opulence and authority paled in comparison to the Red Menace that cowed them even from afar. Like dandelions, they spread to the urban municipalities of our country. Despite the pleasures that surrounded them, the peaceful life of OlorençaNo, it was Tirsmora, altered with their presence and the trouble that they brought along. I remember it quite well. These strangers came from the Far East, nothing quite like here to be sure, but as stated, they were the odd ones out here. Having no held concept or grasp of Trismorés put them at a disadvantage; others who had some knowledge got by.

[sub][i]```A recordação vai estar com ele aonde for
A recordação vai estar pra sempre aonde eu for...```[/i][/sub]

Inevitably, their presence stirred whispers in the taverns and cafés where once only the soft clinking of cups was heard. Some citizens welcomed them, eager to learn their tongue or trade, while others bristled at the mere sight of their banners. My brother, ever the patriot, saw them as a blemish upon the capitals honorlesser shadows under the looming specter of the Red Menace that even he seemed to fear. But I confess, there was something curious about their ways, something that lingered in the narrow streets of Tirsmora. These visitors reminded us that the city, however eternal it might have seemed, was not beyond change. And change, whether welcomed or resisted, had a way of carving its mark deeper than stone. Hopefully, this won't end up being a change for the worse.
